title: U.S. House · Virginia's 4th District
area: Virginia's 4th Congressional District (Richmond, Petersburg, and surrounding areas)

context.text: The Democratic primary was canceled and incumbent Jennifer McClellan advanced unopposed. The Republican Party primary was canceled because no candidates filed; Robert Murray Jr. is the Republican general-election nominee.

summary.text: Jennifer McClellan is the Democratic incumbent U.S. Representative for Virginia's 4th District, first elected in a 2023 special election to succeed the late Rep. A. Donald McEachin. An attorney by training, she spent about two decades in elected office in Richmond, serving in the Virginia House of Delegates and then the Virginia Senate, before going to Congress. She sits on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and is seeking re-election.

background.text: Born in Petersburg, Virginia, in 1972 to parents who worked at Virginia State University (her father as a professor, her mother as a counselor), according to her official biography. She attended Matoaca High School in Chesterfield County, where she was valedictorian.
Earned a B.A. in English and political science from the University of Richmond in 1994 and a J.D. from the University of Virginia School of Law in 1997.
Worked as an associate at the law firm Hunton & Williams and as assistant general counsel at Verizon before her career in elected office.
First elected to the Virginia House of Delegates in 2005; represented District 71 until 2017.

Elected to the Virginia State Senate in 2017, succeeding A. Donald McEachin after he was elected to Congress; represented District 9 until 2023. Her official biography says she passed more than 370 pieces of legislation over eighteen General Assembly sessions, including bills on voting rights, climate change, reproductive health care and workers' protections.
Won a 2023 special election to fill the seat left by McEachin's death; her official biography says she became the first Black woman elected to Congress from Virginia.

In the 119th Congress she serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, including its Communications and Technology and Energy subcommittees; in the 118th Congress she served on the Armed Services and Science, Space, and Technology committees.
According to her official biography, she lives in Richmond with her husband, David Mills, and their two children.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, including its Subcommittees on Communications and Technology and on Energy, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

summary.text: Robert Murray Jr. is the Republican nominee for Virginia's 4th Congressional District, chosen by his party at a July caucus, and is challenging Democratic incumbent Jennifer McClellan. Little biographical information about him is available in public sources reviewed for this guide.

background.text: Became the Republican nominee for the 4th District after a party caucus in July 2026; the Republican primary scheduled for August 4 was canceled.

summary.text: Joan Bell is an independent candidate running in Virginia's 4th Congressional District general election against Democratic incumbent Jennifer McClellan. Ballotpedia lists no biography, prior offices or Candidate Connection survey response for her.

background.text: Qualified for the November 3, 2026 ballot as an independent; she is listed with no prior office and no reported campaign contributions as of Ballotpedia's latest campaign finance data.
